Name: Assessment of staff capacity and contract services related to the department of parks and recreation.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York in relation to an assessment of staff capacity and contract services related to the department of parks and recreation

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Press Conference

Summary: This bill would require the Department of Parks and Recreation (DPR), to submit an annual report that would analyze how the contracting of various parks services affects the performance of its functions. The report would include the number of full-time and part-time staff employed by DPR and assess the department’s contracting requirements, whether the staff headcount is sufficient to meet the needs of the department, and whether it would be feasible to supplement or replace certain contracted work with the addition of more full-time or part-time staff employed by the department.

\pard\ltrpar\nowidctlpar\hyphpar0\fi720\sl480\slmult1\qj\fs24 Section 1. \cf0 Chapter 1 of title 18 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 18-171 to read as follows:\par
\pard\ltrpar\hyphpar0\fi720\sl480\slmult1\qj\ul\'a7 18-171\cf1  Report on staffing and contracting capacity. a. No later than October 1, 2027 and every October 1 thereafter, the department shall submit a report to the mayor and the speaker of the council regarding the allocation of its staff, and an analysis of how the contracting of various parks services affects the performance of its functions. Such report shall include, but need not be limited to:\par
1. The number of full-time and part-time staff employed by the department on July 1 of the current fiscal year, disaggregated by job title and work category and the funding allocation for such staff;\par
2. An assessment of whether the staff headcount is sufficient to meet the needs of the department;\par
3. An assessment of the department\rquote s contracting requirements, including the total number of current contracts, contract duration and the value of such contracts, disaggregated by contract category; and\par
4. An assessment of where it would be feasible to supplement or replace certain contracted work with the addition of more full-time or part-time staff employed by the department and whether any cost or time efficiencies could be generated through the hiring of such staff;\par
b. To prepare the report and assessment required pursuant to subdivision a of this section the department shall consider various factors, including but not limited to;\par
1. Whether work performed by staff employed by the department might be performed more expeditiously than work performed by contracted entities;\par
2. Whether there have been recurring issues with certain contract categories or with specific contractors that have resulted in cost increases or have hindered the department\rquote s ability to perform its functions;\par
3. The department\rquote s historical staffing levels, including both full-time and part-time staff, and the total amount of work contracted out to third-parties;\par
4. Whether the department\rquote s current equipment stock is sufficient, and how equipment needs inform the department\rquote s decision whether to perform work internally or to bid out contracts for services; and\par
5. The challenges that the department may face when replacing contracted services with additional full-time or part-time staff.\par
\pard\cbpat2\ltrpar\fi720\sl480\slmult1\qj\ulnone\'a7 2. This local law takes effect immediately.\fs27\par
